object_context: Type-I blow-up-classification child for Clay statement (A). Audit whether dynamics-specific critical compactness/minimal-element logic can bridge Albritton–Barker finite-I ancient limits to an exact Liouville/backward-uniqueness trigger without importing a global critical topology that finite I has not supplied. Type-II is out of scope and remains open.
structural_coordinates: unforced whole-space 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes; nu normalized to 1
parabolic scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), p_lambda=lambda^2 p(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
Albritton–Barker Type-I quantity I=sup over parabolic cylinders of A+C+D+E; finite I is local scale-invariant control, not a registered global critical Banach norm
blow-up extraction yields a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with I<infinity under the source theorem
suitable-weak compactness gives local strong L3 velocity convergence and local weak L3/2 pressure convergence after subsequence extraction
pressure localization splits pressure into a localized Calderon-Zygmund term plus a harmonic remainder; the latter carries nonlocal/far-field information
global Liouville trigger in Albritton–Barker Theorem 1.2 requires a backward sequence with uniformly bounded global L3 norms
critical-element/profile-decomposition methods require a bounded sequence in a specified global critical topology and control loss of compactness by translations/dilations inside that topology
space translation and dilation are noncompact symmetries; tail escape/profile leakage can preserve all fixed compact-set limits while changing global critical mass
backward-uniqueness routes require exact hypotheses on the limiting solution/vorticity and cannot be invoked from local suitable convergence alone
exact backward self-similar substitution changes the PDE to the Leray stationary equation with drift/dilation; a general ancient solution satisfies the original time-dependent Navier–Stokes system
Type-II singularities need a different normalization/classification mechanism because the Type-I I<infinity class is unavailable

target_interface.input: hypothetical Type-I singular suitable weak solution near (x*,T*)
target_interface.local_limit_output: nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution v on R^3 x (-infinity,0) with I<infinity
target_interface.desired_rigidity_input: either sup_k ||v(t_k)||_L3(R3)<infinity for t_k->-infinity, or another exactly matched global rigidity hypothesis
target_interface.audit_question: Does the local compactness/nontriviality package itself supply the global critical tightness needed by minimal-element/profile or backward-uniqueness rigidity?

solved_analogues.fact: a mild ancient solution with uniformly bounded global L3 norm along a backward sequence is zero
critical-element/profile-decomposition machinery proves the L-infinity_t L3_x criterion and constructs minimal singular data under a global critical-space framework
critical L-infinity_t L3_x regularity is established via backward-uniqueness machinery

near_solved_analogues.fact: Type-I singularity is equivalent to existence of a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with finite I; this supplies the ancient class but not Theorem-1.2's global L3 sequence
bounded local L3 velocity and L3/2 pressure yield local strong/weak compactness and persistence of singularities

method_transfers.source_context: global critical L3 or critical Besov solution sequences
required_assumptions: uniform bound in an explicitly named global critical topology
stability/orthogonality sufficient to pass nonlinear evolution
a minimality functional whose infimum is positive and achieved modulo symmetries
target_disanalogies: finite I is a local cylinder supremum and does not itself bind the global L3 tail
local strong L3 convergence on compact sets does not preclude translated/dilated profiles escaping to infinity
pressure harmonic remainders are not encoded by a velocity-only local compactness statement

required_assumptions: exact terminal-time/decay or global critical hypotheses of the selected theorem
sufficient regularity of vorticity/coefficient fields on the domain where unique continuation is applied
global/exterior control needed to propagate vanishing
target_disanalogies: finite I plus local convergence does not automatically provide the required global terminal/exterior conditions
nontrivial ancient limit need not vanish at t=0 unless a separate blow-up normalization/decay argument proves it

required_assumptions: exact self-similar representation and profile hypotheses
target_disanalogies: general Type-I ancient trajectories are time-dependent
self-similar variables introduce drift/dilation terms and a stationary Leray equation

adversarial_constructions: translation escape: a bounded global critical profile translated to |x_n|->infinity converges strongly to zero on every fixed compact set while retaining global norm
multi-profile leakage: orthogonal translation/dilation parameters can preserve local compactness of the selected core while other profiles carry critical mass
harmonic-pressure remainder: localized Calderon-Zygmund pressure convergence does not determine the global harmonic/far-field component
equation mismatch: a theorem for stationary Leray profiles cannot be applied to arbitrary original-equation ancient solutions
